links.comparator_used: Leakage scenarios without deduplication (duplicates retained) and with random image-level splitting, compared against the clean scenario (deduplicated, patient-level split) across 20 paired repeats
links.outcome: Internal AUC inflation from data leakage in TB detection from chest radiographs
links.effect: Three-class multi-source corpus: AUC saturated near 0.997 in every scenario, paired leakage effects below 0.1 percentage points. Single-source drug-resistance probe: random image-level splitting inflated internal AUC by 1.7 points (95% CI 0.9 to 2.4; p = 0.001), or 1.2 points after a deduplication gap was repaired.
links.quote: On the three-class multi-source corpus, the area under the curve (AUC) saturated near 0.997 in every scenario, consistent with source-class confounding; paired leakage effects were statistically detectable but below 0.1 percentage points.

design_hint: data-governance workflow with deduplication and patient-level splitting
